top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu, single laureate) is the strongest proposal on the common criteria. The voice is distinctive, the formal and linguistic ambition is sustained at large scale, and the imaginative depth is substantial. As publicly described, Blinding (the first volume of the Orbitor trilogy) and Solenoid build memory, the body and dream into one metaphysical architecture. Attribution is clean: one author, one principal language. The citation is best anchored in the prose, the Orbitor trilogy and Solenoid, and should not claim the poetry or early work, which the committee has not assessed. I give no weight to the unanimous support as merit. The reservations remain open. I cannot verify the Romanian prose rhythm and density directly. I do not know whether the later novels transform the project or only extend it. Translation and corpus-coverage limits apply to every candidate. P000 (no award) is ranked last because the proposal is a defensible single-writer case and the open questions narrow the citation without defeating it. This judgment rests on public knowledge and translated reception, not on a full reading or independent verification.
recusal_note: none apparent from the profile; her ties to colleagues (election alongside Steve Sem-Sandberg in 2020, work with chair Anders Olsson, marriage to Pär Nuder) and her Alfred Nobel biography do not connect to the shortlisted writer. Her voting status as a co-opted member is undocumented, so her simulated vote is a modeling assumption.
